CHANGED 2026-07-27: 60 -> 70. After adding SYNTH_NO_FLAT=1, a real
run's log directly reported [GPL-0302] Target density 0.6000 is too
low for the available free area -- raising this based on that

CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
CHANGED 2026-07-26: real hardening data showed WNS of -14.2ns at the
default 20ns period, implying an actual critical path around ~34ns
(~29MHz max). Raised to 100ns (10MHz) for comfortable margin so
timing-repair converges quickly instead of grinding for hours right
at the edge of feasibility. This is the field that actually controls
the synthesis/STA timing constraint -- info.yaml's clock_hz is only
datasheet metadata and does not affect hardening at all.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
CHANGED 2026-07-27: lowered from 0.1/0.05 -- real hardening log
showed thousands of auto-inserted hold-fix/fanout-fix repair
cells (named hold####, fanout####) that OpenROAD couldn't find
legal placement for post-CTS, causing DPL-0036. 8x4 already
confirmed sufficient for the raw design area (utilization check
passed cleanly), so this isn't a size problem -- it's the sheer
number of repair cells these margins are forcing. Lowering the
margin asks for less slack cushion, which should need fewer
inserted buffers.
SYNTH_MAX_FANOUT - added 2026-07-27. A real hardening run showed
thousands of auto-inserted hold-fix/fanout-fix repair cells post-
CTS with nowhere left to place them (DPL-0036). This matches a
documented OpenLane issue (github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenLane
issue #870): large fanouts on mux-heavy structures aren't always
properly capped during synthesis, cascading into exactly this kind
of late, hard-to-fix explosion. RV32 cores are extremely mux-heavy
(regfile read, ALU operand select, immediate select, load/store
byte muxes), making this a plausible match. Setting this forces
fanout-splitting during synthesis itself, spread naturally through
the design, instead of OpenROAD discovering the problem much later.
SYNTH_NO_FLAT - added 2026-07-27. Real logs showed every cell
prefixed $flatten\u_soc..., confirming the entire SoC (core +
accelerator + bus + memory + debug) gets merged into one giant
netlist before synthesis/optimization even starts. A comparative
test against a real, proven reference RISC-V TT project (tinyQV,
which keeps modules naturally small/separate) passed in 20 minutes
while ours ran over an hour without even reaching routing --
pointing at this exact issue. This is OpenLane's own documented fix
for it: postpone flattening until after synthesis/mapping/
optimization, so each module gets optimized separately (much
cheaper for tools like ABC) instead of one enormous merged blob.
PL_MAX_DISPLACEMENT_X/Y - added 2026-07-27. Full run logs showed
CTS itself succeeds (879 clock buffers built cleanly across a real
7-level H-tree), but the legalization pass immediately after fails
for 35 cells -- ALL specifically inside u_soc.u_mem (our memory
module), not scattered across the chip. This is a localized
packing problem near the densely-packed memory flip-flop array,
not a whole-chip density issue. The failing log's own command
showed "-max_displacement 500 100" -- the tool's defaults, unused.
Widening the legalizer's search radius (especially Y, the more
restrictive default) gives it more room to find legal spots.
GPL_CELL_PADDING/DPL_CELL_PADDING - added 2026-07-27. Two
consecutive real runs now show the exact same localized failure:
a small number of cells (35, then 38) fail legal placement, almost
all specifically inside u_soc.u_mem, each time triggered by a
DIFFERENT later stage needing to insert a few new cells nearby
(CTS clock buffers last time, antenna-repair diodes/jumpers this
time). PL_MAX_DISPLACEMENT alone got the first case through but the
same underlying tightness resurfaced at the next stage. Adding
padding around every cell from the start (not just widening the
legalizer's search radius after the fact) should leave consistent
breathing room near the memory for whatever needs to land there
next. Docs note Sky130 libraries typically want DPL_CELL_PADDING
around 4-6; DPL_CELL_PADDING must not exceed GPL_CELL_PADDING.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
